_note: Standing constraint recorded in CLAUDE.md: roughly 8B parameters overall, router included. default_max_params is the SUPERVISOR'S STANDING NUMBER (8e9) and is what any component without its own key inherits - today retrieval, ner and reranker (src/model_size.py _LIMIT_KEY). A role that has been granted an exception gets its OWN key, so the exception cannot spread to a role no ADR admits: that is why answerer_max_params exists (ADR 0019) and, since 2026-09-14, why decomposer_max_params does too (PR for issue #50, review I-1). Asserted in src/model_size.py at every model load; load_limits() requires every key here at startup, dry runs included, so a missing key fails loudly rather than only on a real run (ADR 0016). Changing a number here is Jahid's decision with his supervisor - not an agent's, and not a workaround for a model that fails the assertion.
_decomposer_note: The decomposer's OWN key, and the only one above the standing 8e9. History: raised 8e9 -> 1e10 by Jahid on 2026-08-19 to admit Qwen3.5-9B (ADR 0015), then 1e10 -> 1.5e10 on 2026-09-14 to admit Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct at 14,770,033,664 parameters (ADR 0031 item 4), which Jahid confirmed in his own words on 2026-09-20 - "The limit threshold for the parameter size is also increased" (ADR 0032 item 2). UPDATE 2026-10-14: the supervisor approved the 1.5e10 decomposer exception (relayed by Jahid, ADR 0035 item 6); the remainder of this note is the history. Before that, both raises were PENDING SUPERVISOR CONFIRMATION - ADR 0031's has a recorded supervisor utterance behind it and Jahid has now confirmed it himself, but neither a suggestion to try a larger model in one experiment nor Jahid's own agreement is the act of resetting the thesis's standing size constraint, which CLAUDE.md reserves to the supervisor. If he reasserts 8B or 10B, that supersedes: the revert is this one line, and it touches no other role. Until 2026-09-14 the decomposer shared default_max_params, which meant each raise silently lifted the ceiling for retrieval, ner and reranker as well - inert in practice (largest model in those roles is Jean-Baptiste/roberta-large-ner-english, ~355M) but exactly the spread _answerer_note argues against, so the key was split out. Verify a count against a ceiling with scripts/print_model_params.py.
_answerer_note: The MuSiQue answering backend's reader (issue #16, ADR 0019) gets its OWN key at 8e9 rather than sharing default_max_params. ADR 0015's raise to 1e10, and ADR 0031's to 1.5e10, were each granted for the decomposer role only - and letting the reader inherit them would silently extend that exception to a role no ADR admits. So the reader stays under the standing ~8B ceiling: the default reader (Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3, ~7.25B) passes, and a 9B reader is refused at load time until Jahid records an extension for it. Raising this number is his decision with his supervisor.
